target_customer: Indian businesses, including field heavy enterprises, that pay employee expenses
problem: Employees pay business expenses out of pocket and wait for reimbursement; companies lack real time control. CashBook issues UPI wallets to employees with limits and tracking.
business_model: SaaS pricing per wallet or employee, with wallets issued by a licensed PPI partner

founders.name: Vivek Kumar
previous_startups: Raseedbook (billing and record keeping app, co-founded with Ashutosh Pathak)
founders.background_notes: Per a search summary he previously ran a laundromat and restaurant; this is not verified by a second source.

competitors.name: Happay
competitors.what: Indian corporate card and expense management platform

competitors.name: Zaggle
competitors.what: Mumbai spend management fintech with prepaid cards and expense automation (XPNS)
competitors.traction_then: Founded 2011 per CB Insights; undated page

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs wallet and UPI integration with a licensed issuer and accounting sync with Zoho and Tally, standard fintech engineering with regulatory dependence.

defensibility.rationale: Relies on a partner's PPI licence; rivals can offer cards or wallets with similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Happay was acquired by MakeMyTrip in November 2024 per CB Insights; no incumbent copying of CashBook found.

market_need_then: India's businesses reimburse employee expenses manually and UPI was widely adopted; the founders' earlier Raseedbook app served small business bookkeeping, and CashBook says it serves 4,500+ businesses.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical, positions as UPI native

brand_strength.rationale: App Store listing notes users misspell the name, and several unrelated CashBook apps exist, so the generic name competes for attention.

pivots.from: Mobile app for small businesses to track income and expenses
pivots.why: Sources do not state a reason or exact date

outcome_analysis: CashBook raised a $2.3M seed in September 2021 after YC and is still operating, claiming 4,500+ business customers. UPI adoption in India gave it a tailwind, but its dependence on a partner's wallet licence and the absence of later announced rounds make its long term trajectory unclear.
notes: Seed confirmed by Business Standard and Business Today and others. Founder bios from a search summary of YourStory style profiles; the laundromat and restaurant detail and Alluzo are unverified. Startupintros gave $2M, an outlier. Competitor pages are undated vendor blogs.
